newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-HK newspaper headlines - Sept 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-HK newspaper headlines - Sept 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS -- Protest ship carrying 17 sets off to disputed Diaoyu (Senkaku) islands yesterday in the hope of landing on the islands.

-- Since the Government tightened control over putting up posters in streets, some companies were looking for cheaper means to advertise, including using teenagers to act as mobile advertisement boards.
-- MING PAO -- Nominees for the Selection Committee had started to canvass votes by telephoning, meeting and writing to members of the Preparatory Committee.

-- Many university students in China were doing business in their spare time and student bookstores were popular on the campuses. Books were often spread out on the lower deck of the bunk beds in the dormitories.
-- Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin inspected the regions along the Beijing-Guangzhou railway and urged that Hong Kong's prosperity should be maintained after the handover.
-- The three armed services of the Chinese army carried out a military exercise on September 13 and 14, practicing landing on islands.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- China's World Trade Centre, in which ShangriLa Asia Ltd has 50 per cent stake, was planning to seeking listing overseas.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- The Government has approved that the buildings on the Hunghom Bay recovered land owned by Sun Hung Kai Properties and Henderson Land Development could be as high as 155 metres. The development was expected to boost property prices.
-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Seven of the nine dolphins born at Ocean Park since 1989 have died and park management has admitted that survival rates were "very poor.
-- Nearly 100 Chinese parliamentarians had written to the Communist Party and government leadership on the importance of protecting native industry.
-- CNT Group, the paint, property and bus company controlled by Tsui Tsin-tong, had confirmed it was examining a possible spin-off of its Citybus subsidiary.
-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- The Government was considering setting an examination for foreign barristers as part of its grand plan to fully liberalise legal services.
